criteria.criterion: AC-1: Analyze at least 10 investigation JSONs from the n=100 run — identify patterns in high-D1 hits vs misses
criteria.evidence: docs/spike-investigation-harness.md Appendix A lists 25 commits; 28 commit prefixes in doc map to files under output/runs/2026-06-10_11-39-59_real_n100/investigations/ (100 JSONs on disk). Sections 1.3–1.7 document D1 hit/miss matrix (buggy HIGH=43/MEDIUM=6/LOW=1), hedging catalog, D3 spectrum with quoted reasoning from f897d46, 90846b5, 6bb9f555, b4c933b7f958. Cross-run table §1.2 verified against both eval-report.json files: n100 D1=0.86, n5 D1=0.40, buggy_cite=66/100.

criteria.criterion: AC-2: Research at least 3 external approaches to commit-risk or code-review agents
criteria.evidence: Section 2 documents 6 sources across 4 tracks: Kamei JIT-SDP (2013), CodeRabbit severity rubric, Greptile v3 agentic review, SpotBugs finding structure, Wei CoT (2022), G-Eval. Each has Approach/Relevant/Transferable/Not-applicable subsections. Section 2.5 analogy mapping table satisfies EC-2.

criteria.criterion: AC-3: Builder proposes 3 candidate prompt architectures with rationale
criteria.evidence: Section 3 defines Architecture A (rubric), B (staged CoT), C (adversarial self-critique). Each includes template sketch, expected D1/D3 impact table, cost estimate, and risks. Comparison matrix §3.4 contrasts all three.

criteria.criterion: AC-4: Evaluator critiques each candidate — weaknesses, cost, D1/D3 impact
criteria.evidence: Section 4 scores each architecture on 5 axes (1–5) with specific helps/fails commit citations (f897d46, b4c933b7f958, 90846b5). Verdicts: A=GO, B=GO, C=DEFER. Appendix B documents builder-evaluator dialogue with rebuttals. llm-skeptic check §4 explicitly asks whether regex could do 80% — concludes A justified for D1, B required for D3. Not rubber-stamp: b4c933b7 D3=1.0/D1=0.0 divergence flagged.
File exists at docs/spike-investigation-harness.md (639 lines). Contains executive summary, data analysis, external research, 3 architectures, evaluator critique, recommendation, 3 appendices.

criteria.criterion: AC-6: Recommendation includes specific prompt text or template
criteria.evidence: Section 5.2 provides copy-paste system prompt (~450 words) with four STAGE labels, rubric tiers HIGH/CRITICAL/MEDIUM/LOW, hedge-ban rules, two few-shot examples, JSON schema. Section 5.3 specifies router_probability injection format.

criteria.criterion: AC-7: No code changes — spike is research only
criteria.evidence: git status --short: only docs/spike-investigation-harness.md (new) and .harness/* modified. git diff HEAD -- src/ tests/ returns empty. No orchestrator.py or other source changes.

edge_cases.case: EC-1: n=100 data from leaked run — analysis must account for buggy label influence
edge_cases.evidence: Section 1.1 explicitly labels n=100 as leaked, reports 66/100 reasoning cites buggy (verified programmatically). EC-1 handling paragraph discounts classification driven by buggy=True. Cross-run §1.2 uses n5 clean run to isolate label effect on f897d46/90846b5.

edge_cases.case: EC-2: External research may not find direct commit-risk agent precedent
edge_cases.evidence: Section 2.5 'Analogy Mapping Table' maps JIT-SDP→router, CodeRabbit→rubric, SpotBugs→findings format, Greptile→iter-3. Opening of §2.5 states no direct commit-risk agent precedent exists.

findings.evidence: Section 4 llm-skeptic check: 'Could regex/rubric do 80%?' — concludes D1 partial via rubric, D3 requires LLM. Architecture C deferred as expensive.
Recommendation A+B hybrid: rubric for classification floor (partially deterministic criteria), staged CoT for hypothesis generation (requires semantic diff understanding).
